item.title: Hong Kong taxi driver, 83, acquitted of swearing at passenger, refusing to print fare receipt
item.description: An octogenarian Hong Kong taxi driver accused of being rude to a passenger and refusing to print a receipt last year has been found not guilty. Yen Ken-hoi, 83, appeared at Kowloon City Magistrates’ Courts on Monday to hear the verdict. He earlier denied charges of refusing or neglecting to issue a taxi fare receipt […]

item.title: China conducts 2nd day of military drills around Taiwan
item.description: By James Edgar, with Isabel Kua in Pingtan and Amber Wang in Taipei China kicked off a second day of live-fire drills around Taiwan on Tuesday, aimed at simulating a blockade of the self-ruled island’s key ports and assaults on maritime targets. item.title: Emergency room visits at Hong Kong public hospitals to increase to HK$400 on Jan 1 amid sweeping fee reform
item.description: Public hospitals in Hong Kong will implement new charges starting from January 1, with Accident and Emergency (A&E) fees more than doubling from HK$180 to HK$400. The new measures, first announced in March, aim to promote the “sustainable development” of the city’s public healthcare system to cope with challenges posed by an ageing population, the […]

item.title: LGBTQ activist Jimmy Sham urges return of same-sex rights bill after lawmaker floats ‘contractual partner’ plan
item.description: LGBTQ activist Jimmy Sham has said he hopes Hong Kong’s incoming lawmakers will push for recognition of same-sex partnerships registered overseas, after a lawmaker proposed an alternative “contractual partner” system to replace a vetoed bill. Sham’s remarks on a Commercial Radio programme on Tuesday followed re-elected lawmaker Reverend Peter Koon’s suggestion of a recognition system […]

item.title: 5 taxi drivers arrested over fake claims to ride-hailing company offering free rides for Tai Po fire victims
item.description: Hong Kong police have arrested five taxi drivers on suspicion of forging records to claim reimbursements from a ride-hailing platform that offered free rides to residents affected by the deadly Tai Po fire. item.title: Reducing gov’t venue partners means ‘more opportunities’ for art groups, Hong Kong culture minister says
item.description: Hong Kong’s culture minister has said a decision to reduce the number of government venue partners is meant to provide “more opportunities” for local arts groups, brushing off censorship concerns. item.description: Hong Kong authorities have completed a disciplinary investigation into a fraudulent drinking water supply contract for government offices, as well as a review of the government’s existing procurement regime.
